relationMerges.rationale: Both ownership periods represent the same Argo-managed acquisition and current ownership of the single Oneta Energy Center asset.
Both milestones describe LS Power's August 15, 2019 announcement of the same Oneta and Carville sale to an Argo-managed vehicle.

rationale: Merge the duplicate Oneta Power production identity into the canonical Oneta Energy Center record. Oklahoma DEQ identifies Oneta Power, LLC as the permittee and operator of the Oneta Energy Center facility, so the two records represent one plant and one Argo investment. LS Power announced the sale to an Argo-managed vehicle on August 15, 2019, FERC reports a November 21, 2019 control-transfer date, and EPA's 2023 facility record identifies Argo Infrastructure Partners LP as the 100% parent. The live Oneta site continues to describe the Broken Arrow plant, and no later sale or pending ownership transfer was identified through August 16, 2026. Remove the unsupported Apollo vehicle wording because the announced Apollo-Argo manager transaction was terminated and never created an Oneta ownership change.

beforeImage.name: Oneta Energy Center
beforeImage.description: Oneta Energy Center is a natural gas-fired combined-cycle generation asset in Oklahoma that sells capacity and energy into wholesale power markets and contracted utility arrangements. The project is an asset-heavy thermal generation facility serving the Southwest Power Pool region rather than retail end users. Public materials describe the plant as a 1,127 MW facility near Broken Arrow, Oklahoma, and Missouri municipal disclosure documents reference contracted capacity from the plant beginning in 2020. LS Power announced in August 2019 that it had agreed to sell Oneta and the Carville project to Argo Infrastructure Partners. Public sources reviewed do not disclose a separate project-company founding year or the current ownership percentages.

milestones.event: LS Power announced the sale of Oneta Energy Center and the Carville project to Argo Infrastructure Partners.
Missouri Joint Municipal Electric Utility Commission documents show contracted capacity from Oneta beginning on June 1, 2020.

afterImage.name: Oneta Energy Center
afterImage.description: Oneta Energy Center is a natural gas-fired combined-cycle power plant in Broken Arrow, Wagoner County, Oklahoma, operated by Oneta Power, LLC. The single-plant business sells electricity and capacity into wholesale markets in the Southwest Power Pool. Its official site describes approximately 1,150 MW of nominal capacity, LS Power's 2019 sale announcement described 1,127 MW, and a FERC asset appendix attributes 1,086 MW for market-based-rate reporting. LS Power announced an agreement to sell Oneta and Carville to an Argo-managed investment vehicle on August 15, 2019; FERC reports a November 21, 2019 control-transfer date. EPA's 2023 facility record identifies Argo Infrastructure Partners LP as the 100% parent. Oneta Power and Oneta Energy Center are the operator and facility identities for one Argo investment, not separate manager-level portfolio companies. No later sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 16, 2026.

milestones.event: LS Power announced an agreement to sell Oneta Energy Center and Carville Energy Center to an investment vehicle managed by Argo Infrastructure Partners, subject to customary approvals.
A FERC asset appendix reports November 21, 2019 as the control-transfer date for Oneta Energy Center; EPA later identified Argo Infrastructure Partners LP as its 100% parent.
Missouri Joint Municipal Electric Utility Commission documents show contracted capacity from Oneta beginning on June 1, 2020.
Oneta Power launched a public website identifying its 1,150 MW combined-cycle facility in Broken Arrow, Oklahoma.
